items.title: Start With Experience, Not Matter or Mind | Michel Bitbol
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Do strong correlations between the brain and consciousness prove that one causes the other?*

Michel Bitbol argues that phenomenology begins more cautiously with lived experience, questioning reductionism without committing to dualism, spiritualism, or metaphysical idealism.

0:00 Is Consciousness Reducible?
0:36 Correlation Does Not Establish Reduction
2:58 Consciousness as the Starting Point
4:51 Methodological vs. Metaphysical Idealism
6:17 Beyond the Separation of Mind and Matter

*Michel Bitbol* is a French researcher in philosophy of science. He is "Directeur de recherche" at CNRS, previously in the Centre de Recherche en Épistémologie Appliquée of École polytechnique. He is now a member of Archives Husserl, École Normale Superieure.

items.title: Can We Know Which Theory of Consciousness Is True? | Jeffrey Mishlove
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Should a theory of consciousness be judged only by whether it is true, or also by what it allows us to understand and do?*

Jeffrey Mishlove argues that metaphysical theories may resist ordinary tests of truth, making their pragmatic value important as well. Yet when comparing the major alternatives, he leans toward idealism and an expansive view of the collective unconscious.

0:00 Truth Value vs. Pragmatic Value
2:22 Does Usefulness Have Anything to Do With Truth?
5:17 Why Search for Theories We Cannot Prove?
7:23 Why Mishlove Leans Toward Idealism
8:21 How Far Does the Collective Unconscious Extend?

*Jeffrey Mishlove* is a parapsychologist with a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and Host and Producer of the New Thinking Allowed YouTube channel. The channel features over 1,500 videos exploring psychology, philosophy, health, science, spirituality, parapsychology, and the paranormal.

items.title: Why It Matters Which Species Go Extinct | Derek Turner
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can fossils help us make better decisions about today's biodiversity crisis?*

Derek Turner says paleontology cannot derive ethical principles from the fossil record, but extinction selectivity may reveal something crucial that extinction rates alone miss: which species are most vulnerable and why.

0:00 Paleontology and the Biodiversity Crisis
2:00 More Than Rates and Magnitudes
3:47 The Ethics of De-Extinction

*Derek Turner* is the Class of '43 Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Goodwin-Niering Center for the Environment at Connecticut College. A recipient of both the John S. King Teaching Award and the Nisbet Rash Research Award, his work focuses on the philosophy of paleontology, macroevolution, and deep time. He is the author of _Paleontology: A Philosophical Introduction_ and _Paleoaesthetics and the Practice of Paleontology,_ as well as a co-founder of the philosophy of paleontology blog _Extinct._

items.title: Why the Argument from Evil Depends on Probability | Michael Tooley
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can the existence of evil make a perfectly good God mathematically improbable?*

Michael Tooley argues that plausible equiprobability principles can assign equal weight to a vast range of possible supernatural beings, dramatically reducing the probability that the being who exists is perfectly good.

0:00 Evidential Arguments from Evil
1:49 The Hypothesis of Indifference
3:56 An Infinity of Possible Beings
8:15 From Best Explanation to Equiprobability
15:12 The Million Marble Argument
19:01 Bayesian Probability and Equal Priors

*Michael Tooley* is Emeritus Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder. He received a Boulder Faculty Assembly Excellence in Research Award in 1998 for his book _Time, Tense, and Causation,_ and is the author of the new book _Causation: A Defense of a Non-Reductionist Approach_ (Oxford, 2026).

items.title: The Problem with Substance Dualism | Alex Gómez-Marín
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Does dualism still deserve a place among theories of consciousness?*

Alex Gómez-Marín respects its refusal to reduce mind, consciousness, or spirit to matter, but argues that substance dualism creates a major problem when two separate substances must somehow interact.

0:00 Beyond the Materialism-Dualism Choice
1:51 Why Dualism Deserves Respect
2:56 The Interaction Problem and Other Alternatives

*Alex Gómez-Marín* is a Spanish physicist turned neuroscientist. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and a Masters in biophysics from the University of Barcelona. He was a research fellow at the EMBL-CRG Centre for Genomic Regulation and at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown in Lisbon. His research spans from the origins of the arrow of time in inert systems, to the neurobiology of action-perception in living organisms such as flies, worms, mice, and humans.

items.title: Could Consciousness Include Everything? | Jeffrey Mishlove
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Could individual minds be part of a consciousness that includes everything?*

Jeffrey Mishlove speculates that consciousness may extend throughout reality and that individual minds could help a larger consciousness become aware of itself, a possibility he connects with both personal conceptions of God and non-personal traditions of consciousness.

items.title: Does the Human Mind Have an Immaterial Component? | Oliver Crisp
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Does Christian theology require something about the human mind to be immaterial?*

Oliver Crisp tentatively favors substance dualism but argues for keeping multiple metaphysical possibilities open, using the Incarnation as a test case for what Christians can say about the relationship between mind, body, and soul.

0:00 The Mind-Body Problem from a Theological Perspective
1:24 Christianity and the Limits of Reductive Materialism
2:33 A Tentative Case for Substance Dualism
3:57 The Incarnation as a Test Case for Human Nature
4:47 Human Nature and the Soul as an Interface

items.title: Could Time and Consciousness Share a Foundation? | Susan Schneider
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if time does not fundamentally have a direction?*

Susan Schneider proposes that reality at the level of quantum entanglement may involve "proto-time," with time's arrow emerging through interaction with the environment, and explores how this idea could support her form of panpsychism.

0:00 Introducing Proto-Time and Superpsychism
1:11 Emergent Spacetime and a Unified Explanation
3:46 Proto-Time, Entanglement, and Time's Arrow
4:59 Proto-Time as a Form of Panpsychism
